title: Big Eye Louis's wife Corrine and the song Corrine
summary: Barnes recalls the one wife he knew Louis to have, Corrine, and says the band played the song 'Corrine, Corrine' because of her.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Was he married once, do you remember, I think somebody told me he was, I never talked to him very much, I made some records once with him, but I never bothered him much, you know, to ask him questions. Do you know, was he ever married? Somebody told me you know who he was.
Well, I don't know. Well, I think he was married to, oh, Corrine. To a Cree?
Didn't Fess tell us something about Corrine?
That was her name. I don't know what. She's going to be dead, yeah. Yes. That was the only wife that I know that he had, but for being married in those days, I don't remember.
In late years, he just lived with his sister, you know.
And I wondered if he'd never had a wife or lived with any woman, I just wondered. Corrine.
That's what the number come out, they used to play, Corrine, Corrine, how long you been gone.

That's the number that come out from that. They used to kill them both. We used to play that song. And they called it, let's play Corrine. You see? So they called it, playing Corrine, Corrine, Corrine. Why has you been too long?
